Here's what to look for on the package 
 Look inside the USDA mark for EST. M/P 7839, P 20935A or M 9520, then check the product list. Here's what to do if yours is recalled
 1 / 7 List slides Is your bacon or hot dog in the Kayem recall? Here's what to look for on the package List slides Previous Start over By Colleen Cabili · Updated October 23, 2026 Add QZ to Google Mateusz Feliksik / Unsplash
 Kayem Foods, the Chelsea, Massachusetts maker of Fenway Franks, Al Fresco chicken sausage and McKenzie deli meats, recalled about 1.58 million pounds of ready-to-eat hot dogs, bacon, deli meats and sausages on October 17 because some of it may not have been kept cold enough in storage. It covers products sold in grocery stores and to restaurants and other foodservice customers.
 The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service announced the recall and classified it Class I, its highest-risk category, though there are no confirmed reports of illness. FSIS's recall notice says the products carry one of three establishment numbers inside the USDA mark of inspection, and the five slides below show how to check a package and what to do if yours is affected.
 What was recalled and why 
 Marshalok Brend / Unsplash
 Kayem is recalling 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products, produced approximately March 31 through October 7, 2026 and shipped to retail and foodservice locations nationwide and to Hong Kong. FSIS gave the recall its Class I designation, which it defines as a situation where there is a reasonable probability that using the product will cause serious adverse health consequences or death.
 The problem surfaced on October 1, when Kayem received a retail customer complaint about warm product temperatures at delivery. The company found that it had stored various products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations, and the notice doesn't name a specific contaminant.
 Check the brand and the product 
 S. Laiba Ali / Unsplash
 Start with the brand. The recalled products were sold under the names Al Fresco, Deutschmacher, Essem, Jordan's, Kayem, McKenzie, Triple M and Winnisimmet, among others, according to AARP's summary of the notice.
 The list is long, covering more than 45 types of products according to NBC News. Hot dogs and franks, including beef, lower-sodium, skinless and red varieties and Fenway Franks, are on it, as are bacon in thick-cut, applewood-smoked, maple and slab varieties, ham, turkey breast, bologna, kielbasa, bratwurst, beef brisket, corned beef, chicken sausage, meatballs and liverwurst.
 Find the establishment number 
 0xk / Unsplash
 Turn the package over and look inside the USDA mark of inspection for an establishment number. The recalled products bear one of three: EST. M/P 7839, EST. P 20935A or EST. M 9520.
 On the recall's product list, for example, McKenzie's black forest uncured ham is listed with EST. 9520 and McKenzie's hickory smoked turkey breast with EST. P-20935A. A package without one of these three numbers isn't covered by the recall as announced, and a package with one should be checked against the product list.
 Match the UPC and the dates 
 COSMOH / Unsplash
 FSIS published the product labels and a list of products with their UPC codes , and the UPC printed under the barcode on your package is the easiest thing to match. The list also shows expiration and production dates for each item, according to local news coverage.
 Dates alone can mislead. FSIS lists production dates of approximately March 31 through October 7, while Kayem has described a storage and shipping window of June 7 through October 14, so use the product list rather than a date range. Because products also went to foodservice customers, the recall may touch prepared items from delis and cafeterias, and FSIS says it will post retail distribution lists when they are available.
 What to do if yours is recalled 
 Nicolas J. Barbier / Unsplash
 FSIS urges anyone who bought the products not to eat them and to throw them away or return them to the store where they were purchased. The agency says it is concerned some product may still be in consumers' refrigerators, and no one has confirmed an illness from the recall so far. Anyone concerned about an illness should contact a health care provider.
 Kayem's customer service line is 800-426-6100, and its email is [email protected] . The USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline, at 888-674-6854 or [email protected] , answers food safety questions, and problems with a meat, poultry or egg product can be reported through FSIS's online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System.
